messages:
Taylor (sec): quick sync — need a concise oncall playbook for AWS KMS when we run Redwood Private in customers' VPCs. specifically: control-plane CMKs, data-plane DEKs, rotation, and incident steps for compromised CMKs.
Ravi: +1. we should make two separate flows: 1) control-plane CMK (customer-managed or our keystore?) and 2) per-tenant data-plane DEK envelope keys.
Taylor (sec): agreed. for Private we assume customer wants BYOK or customer-managed CMK in their account. outline should cover grants, cross-account roles, and audit/log correlation.
Maria (platform): i'm worried about RBAC changes during rotation — we need a safe window where old key still decrypts and new key is used for encrypt. canonical approach: rewrap DEKs with new CMK asynchronously and keep version metadata.
Sam (oncall): for paging: what triggers an oncall page? KMS throttling vs key compromised vs missing DEK? we need runbook bullets.
Ali (infra): propose TL;DR runbook snippets in the playbook: 1) validate CloudTrail events for kms:Decrypt/GenerateDataKey 2) check KMS quotas 3) failover to fallback CMK (pre-approved) 4) if compromised, revoke grants and rotate KEK + rewrap.
Ravi: adding notes about grants: avoid long-lived IAM key policies; use KMS grants scoped to the control-plane service principal. example grant creation:```bash
aws kms create-grant --key-id alias/redwood-controlplane --grantee-principal arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role/redwood-controlplane --operations "Decrypt" "GenerateDataKey"
```
Ravi: include encryption-context enforcement: we must validate encryption-context = "tenant_id" at decrypt time to avoid cross-tenant decrypt.
Taylor (sec): yep — highlight that encryption-context should be part of DEK lifecycle metadata and logged in CloudTrail. CloudTrail events for Decrypt include encryptionContext; correlate with our app logs.
Maria (platform): sample rewrap command for re-encrypting DEKs with new CMK:```bash
# fetch encrypted DEK, decrypt with old KEK locally via KMS, then re-encrypt with new KEK
aws kms decrypt --ciphertext-blob fileb://enc_DEK.bin --key-id alias/old-kev --encryption-context "{\"tenant\":\"t-123\"}" --output text --query Plaintext | base64 --decode > dek.raw
aws kms encrypt --key-id alias/new-kev --plaintext fileb://dek.raw --encryption-context "{\"tenant\":\"t-123\"}" --ciphertext-blob fileb://enc_DEK_new.bin
```
Ali (infra): operational concerns: KMS throttling during bulk rewrap. recommend rate-limited workers + backoff, and a rewrap batch status endpoint in platform to track progress. also plan for rewrap resume if interrupted.
Sam (oncall): incident scenarios to document:
• KMS CMK schedule rotation collision (two rotations running)
• Cross-account role misconfig => Decrypt failing for control-plane -> pages oncall
• Abuse: suspicious Decrypt calls (unusual principal) -> immediate grant revoke and investigative steps

Sam (oncall): for suspicious Decrypt calls, procedure:
1) check CloudTrail event: eventName == Decrypt or GenerateDataKey 
2) check userIdentity and invokedBy fields, and encryptionContext
3) if principal not recognized: use aws kms revoke-grant + disable key (If customer-managed, open support channel)
4) set failover to fallback CMK alias/redwood-fallback for control-plane operations (needs pre-granted access)

Ravi: sample revoke flow:```bash
# list grants
aws kms list-grants --key-id alias/redwood-controlplane
# revoke grant
aws kms revoke-grant --key-id alias/redwood-controlplane --grant-id <grant-id>
# optionally disable key (if CMK in our account)
aws kms disable-key --key-id <key-id>
```
Taylor (sec): note: disabling customer-managed CMKs we can't do without customer approval — include clear customer communication template in playbook.
Maria (platform): audit logging: ensure control-plane has structured logs with fields: tenant_id, operation, key_alias, request_id, request_trace_id. correlate request_trace_id with CloudTrail eventId. include query examples for Splunk/Datadog.
Ali (infra): quick Splunk query suggestion: `index=aws_cloudtrail eventName=Decrypt AND userIdentity.arn=\"arn:aws:iam::*:role/redwood-controlplane\" | stats count by sourceIPAddress, encryptionContext.tenant`
Taylor (sec): rotation strategy bullets we should include:
- KEK rotation cadence (90 days default, customer-controlled)
- DEK TTL for cached DEKs (short: e.g., 6h) to reduce rewrap window
- pre-create new key + schedule grants -> phased rewrap -> retire old key after 2x TTL

Ravi: edgecases: multi-region failover: KMS CMKs are regional. for cross-region control-plane, we need either replicate DEKs (encrypted under region CMK) or use multi-region CMKs (if available) or fallback model. document tradeoffs.
Sam (oncall): add incident playbook checklist at top: quick triage steps, paging rules, escalation matrix, customer notification templates, and post-incident audit tasks.
Taylor (sec): also capture RBAC change workflow: PR in infra-repo that modifies the control-plane role's kms:Decrypt permissions must include a checklist: (1) review grant usage, (2) run integration test in staging that tries GenerateDataKey/Decrypt with encryption-context, (3) signoff from sec + platform.
Ravi: vuln triage note: if a library does accidental plaintext logging of DEKs, immediate step = rotate KEK + force rewrap + invalidate cached DEKs + rotate any session tokens. add forensics steps.
Maria (platform): want a short template for the customer-side onboarding checklist:
- choose CMK model: BYOK vs Redwood-managed
- confirm CloudTrail enabled + logs forwarded to customer/our observability as required
- exchange role ARNs and grant scope
- approve fallback CMK alias and emergency contact

Ali (infra): i can draft the playbook doc and a compact runbook for oncall. timeline: will have first draft by EOD tomorrow.
Taylor (sec): great. Sam, Ravi — can you both review the incident scenarios? also add any red-team discovered attack vectors we should cover.
Sam (oncall): will review tonight and add explicit pager thresholds.
Ravi: will add encryption-context enforcement tests and a sample unit test to prevent regressions.
oncall-bot: reminder — create a follow-up ticket: INFRA-8253 \"KMS oncall playbook + rewrap tooling\" assigned to Ali, due in 3d.
Taylor (sec): cool — action items: Ali draft playbook, Ravi add tests + grant guidance, Sam add pager thresholds, Maria add onboarding checklist & log correlation queries. i'll assemble final doc and circulate. :thumbsup:
